bib.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
bib.venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)

question: Is LLM-generated code really correct, given that the tests in popular code benchmarks like HumanEval are few and weak?
hypothesis: Prior evaluation on HumanEval is not robust enough to detect wrong code synthesized by LLMs, so stronger tests will lower pass rates and can change model rankings.
contributions: Study of test inadequacy in current programming benchmarks
EvalPlus: ChatGPT seed inputs plus type-aware mutation, differential testing against ground truth, optional test-suite reduction, and program input contracts
HumanEval+ (80x tests) and HumanEval+-Mini (47x smaller), evaluation of 26 LLMs, and 18 fixed wrong ground-truth solutions in HumanEval

method.summary: EvalPlus asks ChatGPT for about 30 seed inputs per HumanEval task, mutates them with type-aware mutation for a one-hour budget to get about 1000 more inputs, filters by hand-written contracts, and checks LLM code by differential testing against re-implemented ground truths. 26 LLMs are scored with unbiased pass@k on HumanEval and HumanEval+. Greedy set cover over branch coverage, killed mutants and killed LLM samples gives HumanEval+-Mini.
method.task: Python function-level code generation benchmark evaluation (test augmentation)

datasets.name: HumanEval
datasets.preprocessing: Over 10% of ground-truth solutions found incorrect; all re-implemented for HumanEval+ (18 defects, 11% of problems)

datasets.name: HumanEval+
datasets.size: 164 tasks, avg 764.1 tests per task (Table 2); 80x HumanEval
datasets.preprocessing: About 30 ChatGPT seed inputs from 3 separate prompts per task, then type-aware mutation generating 1000 additional inputs using a one-hour budget; 83 of 164 tasks annotated with hand-crafted contracts

datasets.name: HumanEval+-Mini
datasets.size: avg 16.1 tests per task (47x smaller than HumanEval+)
datasets.preprocessing: Set cover on branch coverage, killed mutants, killed samples of other LLMs (leave-one-out)

models.name: Phind-CodeLlama, WizardCoder-CodeLlama, CodeLlama, StarCoder, CodeGen, CodeGen2, CodeT5+, Mistral, Vicuna, SantaCoder, InCoder, GPT-J, GPT-Neo, PolyCoder, StableLM

inference.decoding: Random sampling at 4 temperatures plus greedy decoding
inference.max_tokens: 512 new tokens by default; 1024 for ChatGPT on tasks with very long problem descriptions
inference.samples: 200 samples per task per temperature; best pass@k over temperatures reported for k in {1,10,100}; greedy gives one sample for pass@1*. GPT-4 greedy only; ChatGPT greedy plus 0.8-temperature sampling
inference.prompting: Model-card default prompts; instruction-wrapped signature plus docstring for ChatGPT, GPT-4, WizardCoder-CodeLlama. Code truncated at HumanEval EOS identifiers and model-specific ones; chat output parsed from code blocks

parameters.mutation_budget: 1000 additional inputs, one-hour budget per task
parameters.test_timeout: max(200ms, 4 x t_gt) per test-case, t_gt = ground-truth runtime
parameters.float_tolerance: absolute difference as annotated in HumanEval, else 1e-6

other.serving: ChatGPT and GPT-4 via OpenAI APIs; CodeGen-6B/16B via NVIDIA FasterTransformer through FauxPilot; others HuggingFace transformers

metrics.name: pass@k (unbiased)
metrics.definition: Unbiased pass@k of Chen et al. 2021; correct if all test inputs return matching outputs within the timeout

metrics.name: pass@1*
metrics.definition: pass@1 with greedy decoding, one deterministic sample per task

eval.protocol: Exact match oracle by differential testing against re-implemented ground truth; leave-one-out cross validation for the sample-killing reducer; no seeds or significance tests reported

availability.data: Enhanced datasets and all LLM-generated code open-sourced at the same repository

evidence.quote: for each model we perform: (i) random sampling to generate 200 program samples for each of the four temperature settings ({0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}); and (ii) greedy-search decoding.

results.claim: HumanEval+ lowers pass@k by up to 19.3-28.9% across the 26 models, depending on k.
results.setup: 26 LLMs, HumanEval vs HumanEval+, 200 samples per temperature, best temperature per k
results.note: Section 3 splits it as 23.1% (pass@1*) / 19.3% (pass@1) / 24.9% (pass@10) / 28.9% (pass@100). The paper does not say whether these are relative or absolute.

results.claim: GPT-4 greedy pass@1* falls from 88.4 to 76.2 on HumanEval+.
results.setup: GPT-4, greedy decoding, HumanEval base vs +extra
results.table: Table 3, row GPT-4, columns k=1* base 88.4 and +extra 76.2

results.claim: ChatGPT pass@1* falls from 73.2 to 63.4 on HumanEval+.
results.table: Table 3, row ChatGPT, column k=1* base 73.2, +extra 63.4

results.claim: Two open 34B CodeLlama fine-tunes beat ChatGPT on HumanEval+ pass@1* but not on HumanEval.
results.setup: Phind-CodeLlama-34B 67.1 and WizardCoder-CodeLlama-34B 64.6 vs ChatGPT 63.4 on HumanEval+; on base, ChatGPT 73.2 equals WizardCoder 73.2 and Phind is 71.3
results.quote: WizardCoder-CodeLlama and Phind-CodeLlama on the original HUMANEVAL are evaluated to be no better than ChatGPT in terms of pass@1⋆. However, HUMANEVAL+ demonstrates that the two open-source models can actually outperform the proprietary ChatGPT.

results.claim: HumanEval+ has about 80x more tests per task than HumanEval.
results.quote: which on average obtains 764.1 tests for each programming task (Table 2)
results.note: Table 4 caption prints 774.8 for HumanEval+ average; Table 2 and text print 764.1.

results.claim: Test-suite reduction yields HumanEval+-Mini with 16.1 tests per task, 47x smaller, with nearly the same pass@1* drop.
results.setup: Greedy set cover over coverage, mutants and other LLMs' sample kills, leave-one-out validation
results.quote: only has 16.1 tests for each task (smaller by 47×)

results.claim: 18 of the 164 original HumanEval ground-truth solutions are defective (11%).
results.setup: Differential testing between re-implemented and original ground truths; 5 unhandled edge case, 10 bad logic, 3 performance
results.quote:
we also found 18 defects (11% of problems) even in the original ground-truth in HU-
MANEVAL
results.note: Section 3 setup says 'over 10%' were incorrectly implemented.

results.claim: Lower temperature works best for small k and higher temperature for larger k; optimal temperatures stay mostly stable after augmentation.

limits: Only HumanEval is augmented; MBPP and other benchmarks are listed as future work.
GPT-4 evaluated with greedy decoding only; ChatGPT with greedy and temperature 0.8 only, for time and cost.
Test-suite reduction validated on a subset of models, for time and space.
No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the reduction percentages are not defined as relative or absolute.
Ground truths were hand re-implemented and 83 of 164 tasks have hand-crafted contracts; no formal verification, and the authors list formal verification as future work.
CodeGen2-16B evaluated from an unfinished checkpoint, greedy only.
